name: Unukalhai
description: A giant of type K2 III 22.7 parsecs away, 11.6 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 140573: radius 11.62 +/- 0.06 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 4.77 +/- 0.013 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax

mass.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 140573: mass 1.61 +/- 0.12 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 140573: effective temperature 4687 +/- 59 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

distance.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 140573: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 44.1 +/- 0.19 mas, inverted

text.card: A giant of type K2 III, 23 parsecs away: 11.6 times the Sun's width and 59 times its light.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 4.77 milliarcseconds, which gives 11.62 solar radii and 4,687 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 140573: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 4429785739602747392 (quality A), from 2005A&A...430..165F; Gaia DR3 measures none
